rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh is an appositive to “the day the two armies met” and a temporal adverb for “We sent down,” locating the descent at their positions on the banks.
rows.anchor: إذ } بدل من { يوم التقى الجمعان } ( الأنفال : 41 ) فهو ظرف ب { لأنزلنا

words: إِذْ أَنتُم بِٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَهُم بِٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلْقُصْوَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The detailed setting recalls a perilous encounter with a well-equipped enemy and highlights God's great care; Quranic geography is recounted for its lesson, not as description alone.
rows.anchor: تنبيههم للطف عظيم حفهم من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun is read with damma by the majority and with kasra by Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub; damma and kasra are the more eloquent forms among the three vowels.
rows.anchor: فقرأه الجمهور بضم العين ، وقرأه ابن كثير ، وأبو عمرو ، و يعقوب بكسر العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The banks are the two shores of the Badr valley, Badr being a water source: the nearer bank faced Medina, while the farther bank toward Mecca was a dune.
rows.anchor: وبدر اسم ماء . { والدنيا } هي القريبة أي العدوة التي من جهة المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The labels near and far do not rank the banks; Muslims had wanted the firmer far bank, so the enemy's arrival there initially dismayed them.
rows.anchor: لأنها أصلب أرضا فليس للوصف بالدنو والقصو أثر في تفضيل إحدى العدوتين على الأخرى

words: إِذْ أَنتُم بِٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَهُم بِٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلْقُصْوَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain packed the Muslims' soft sandy ground so they could move, but made the ground occupied by Quraysh difficult, delaying their march and helping the Muslims reach Badr first.
rows.anchor: أرسل الله المطر وكان الوادي دهسا فلبد المطر الأرض ولم يعقهم عن المسير وأصاب الأرض التي بها قريش فعطلهم عن الرحيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “they” refers to the other gathering, the Quraysh army, understood from the dual “two armies” after the verse addressed the Muslims as “you.”
rows.anchor: وضمير { وهم } عائد إلى ما في لفظ { الجمعان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-rakb is the Quraysh caravan returning from Syria, also called al-ayr; its forty men were traveling on the lower coastal route, leaving Badr's water to their left.
rows.anchor: هو ركب قريش الراجعون من الشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Abu Sufyan learned the Muslims were pursuing his caravan, he turned it from the Badr road onto the coastal route to escape, where it traveled on lower plains.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن أبا سفيان لما بلغه أن المسلمين خرجوا لتلقي عيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muslims lay between Abu Sufyan's force on the far bank and the caravan below them; if the enemy had noticed, it could have trapped them. They hoped to seize the caravan, as 8:7 says.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : والركب بالجهة السفلى منكم ، وهي جهة البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asfal is a locative adverb functioning as the predicate of al-rakb: the caravan had passed below them, although they hoped to catch and plunder it.
rows.anchor: وانتصب { أسفل } على الظرفية المكانية وهو في محل رفع خبر عن ( الركب )

words: إِذْ أَنتُم بِٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَهُم بِٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلْقُصْوَىٰ وَٱلرَّكْبُ أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent odds favored Quraysh: they had strength, water, and firmer ground, while Muslims faced soft sand and little water, and the caravan was safely behind the enemy.
rows.anchor: فإنهم كانوا حينئذ في أشد ما يكون فيه جيش تجاه عدوه

words: إِذْ أَنتُم بِٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَهُم بِٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلْقُصْوَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reversed the situation through rain, water, and the enemy's carelessness, granting victory where Muslims least expected it; recalling the scene prompts gratitude, trust in God's promise, and reliance on Him.
rows.anchor: فكان من عجيب عناية الله بالمسلمين أن قلب تلك الحالة رأسا على عقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clause is circumstantial to the two armies' meeting: they met without arrangement, at one time and in neighboring, facing locations.
rows.anchor: وجملة { ولو تواعدتم لاختلفتم في الميعاد } في موضع الحال من { الجمعان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disagreement in the appointment means one side would be late for the agreed time, so both would not arrive together.
rows.anchor: اختلاف وقته بأن يتأخر أحد الفريقين عن الوقت المحدود فلم يأتوا على سواء

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators supply that the Muslims would have realized their small numbers against the enemy's large force; Ibn Ashur rejects this because it predicts failure to attend, not mismatched timing.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من اضطر إلى تقدير كلام محذوف

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Another proposed that Muslims would learn their weakness and Quraysh would fear them, making one side hesitate; Ibn Ashur says this also implies nonattendance rather than differing appointment times.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قدر : وعلمتم قلتكم وشعر المشركون بالخوف منكم

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators explain the mismatch by ordinary interruptions and contingencies; Ibn Ashur calls this the closest proposal but still not fully satisfying.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من جعل ذلك لما لا يخلو عنه الناس من عروض العوارض والقواطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur reads this as “the Suhaybiyya لو”: the answer remains true whether the condition is imagined or not, either because it is likelier without the condition or regardless of it; he cross-refers to 8:23 and 6:111.
rows.anchor: فالوجه في تفسير هذه الآية أن { لو } هذه من قبيل ( لو ) الصهيبية فإن لها استعمالات ملاكها

rows.speaker: طفيل
rows.claim: Tufayl's praise poem says even a mother enduring the same hardship would not tire, illustrating the construction's point that the result holds all the more in ordinary cases.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا قول طفيل في الثناء على بني جعفر بن كلاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense is that a planned meeting would probably have had unequal arrival times, since appointments then used approximate parts of the day; arriving together without a plan shows God's facilitation and promised victory.
rows.anchor: لأن التوقيت كان في تلك الأزمان تقريبا يقدرونه بأجزاء النهار كالضحى والعصر والغروب

rows.speaker: الأسود بن يعفر
rows.claim: Al-Aswad ibn Ya'far's elegy uses “as if they had an appointment” for sequential events, a different comparison from the verse's hypothetical about missing the same meeting time.
rows.anchor: كما قال الأسود بن يعفر يرثي هلاك أحلافه وأنصاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “you would differ” includes both armies, with the addressees grammatically given precedence over the absent group.
rows.anchor: وضمير { اختلفتم } على الوجوه كلها شامل للفريقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adversative means they did not arrange the meeting but arrived together so God could bring about His intended victory over the polytheists; their coincidence was divinely determined.
rows.anchor: ولكن لم تتواعدوا وجئتم على غير اتعاد ليقضي الله أي ليحقق وينجز ما أراده من نصركم على المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amr here means a great, important affair rather than an ordinary command; its indefinite form magnifies it, and the sense links to 19:21 and 33:38.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { أمرا } هنا الشيء العظيم ، فتنكيره للتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur points to his earlier discussion of “if He had made them hear” in this sura and his treatment of the related construction in al-An'am.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدمت الإشارة إلى هذا عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kana can mark a quality as established from the past, as in 30:47; here “was accomplished” means it was fixed in God's knowledge as certain to occur.
rows.anchor: و { كان } تدل على تحقق ثبوت معنى خبرها لاسمها من الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event is described with a passive participle as if already done: God would enact a great event destined since eternity to occur despite ordinary impediments.
rows.anchor: لينجز الله ويوقع حدثا عظيما متصفا منذ القدم بأنه محقق الوقوع عند إبانه

words: لِّيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَنۢ بَيِّنَةٍۢ وَيَحْيَىٰ مَنْ حَىَّ عَنۢ بَيِّنَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is an explicative appositive to God's bringing about the affair: Muslim victory and defeat of the polytheists entail the perishing of the defeated and revival of the victorious, with clear evidence before both.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { ليهلك من هلك عن بينة } في موضع بدل الاشتمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second purpose lam reinforces the first; without it, yahlik would be nominative rather than subjunctive.
rows.anchor: ودخول لام التعليل على فعل { يهلك } تأكيد للام الداخلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perishing and life figuratively mean loss of strength and a community's rise; their contrast is like 9:42, 36:70, and 6:122, since Muslims were few and Quraysh powerful before Badr.
rows.anchor: والهلاك والحياة مستعاران لمعنى ذهاب الشوكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Badr's outcome visibly demonstrated God's support for one people and abandonment of another, leaving no doubt and no excuse for the defeated while obliging the survivors to give thanks.
rows.anchor: أي عن حجة ظاهرة تدل على تأييد الله قوما وخذله آخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words are figurative rather than literal: literal death could suit yahlik, but not yahya, since the survivors were already alive before Badr.
rows.anchor: ومن البعيد حمل { يهلك } و { يحيى } على الحقيقة لأنه وإن تحمله المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The figurative sense of عن is “after”: destruction and life emerge from, and are manifest through, a clear proof clarifying their causes.
rows.anchor: ودل معنى المجاوزة الذي في { عن } على أن المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi, al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr from Asim, Yaqub, and Khalaf articulate both y sounds in حيي; the remaining readers assimilate one into the other. Both are eloquent.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع ، والبزي عن ابن كثير ، وأبو بكر عن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing description means God heard the Muslims' prayer, discussions about going to Badr, and wish for the unarmed caravan; He also knows their unspoken thoughts and what serves their future glory.
rows.anchor: تذييل يشير إلى أن الله سميع دعاء المسلمين طلب النصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most likely, this sentence coordinates with “among those around you” in 9:101: alongside nearby Bedouin hypocrites were Medinans who had sinned through staying behind and confessed; plural sins and mixed deeds mark believers, not hypocrites.
rows.anchor: الأظهر أن جملة : { وءاخرون اعترفوا } عطف على جملة : { وممن حولكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among them were al-Jadd ibn Qays, Kardam, Aras ibn Tha'laba, Wadi'a ibn Hizam, Mirdas, Abu Qays, and Abu Lubaba, with three others; after staying behind from Tabuk, they repented and tied themselves to mosque pillars until this verse revealed God's pardon.
rows.anchor: وكان من هؤلاء جماعة منهم الجد بن قيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: I'tiraf derives from ʿarafa and intensifies knowing, hence admission and no longer denying; confession of a past sin implies regret and resolve not to repeat it, though withdrawal from a past act is impossible.
rows.anchor: والاعتراف : افتعال من عرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their good deeds were mixed with the wrongs of staying behind from the campaign and failing to contribute expenditure for the army.
rows.anchor: وخلطهم العمل الصالح والسيىء هو خلطهم حسنات أعمالهم بسيئات التخلف عن الغزو وعدم الإنفاق على الجيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coordinating the two objects with waw treats them equally as participants in mixing; the alternative “mixing one with the other” means the same, but the coordinated wording is clearer and more eloquent.
rows.anchor: جاء ذكر الشيئين المختلطين بالعطف بالواو على اعتبار استوائهما في وقوع فعل الخلط عليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God's words to the Prophet, “perhaps” is a metonym for assured fulfillment—God has accepted their repentance—while retaining the nuance of the speaker's choice about whether it occurs.
rows.anchor: وهي من كلام الله تعالى المخاطب به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهي كناية عن وقوع المرجو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's turning to them means accepting their repentance, as Ibn Ashur discussed at 2:37.
rows.anchor: ومعنى : { أن يتوب عليهم } أي يقبل توبتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement that God is forgiving and merciful is a coda well suited to this context.
rows.anchor: إن الله غفور رحيم } تذييل مناسب للمقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a corrupter seeks immediate gain, Shuayb follows his warning by pointing to God's reward for obedience, a lasting benefit better than fleeting goods.
rows.anchor: وإذ قد كانت غاية المفسد من الإفساد اجتلاب ما فيه نفع عاجل له من نوال ما يحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqiyya can mean permanence and imply its opposite, passing away: worldly goods vanish, while the good God calls people toward endures in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: ولفظ { بقيت } كلمة جامعة لمعان في كلام العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawful earnings rest on natural and rightful entitlement and mutual consent, preventing resentment, hostility, and retaliation, and preserving a society's security.
rows.anchor: فأما كونه دنيويا فلأن الكسب الحلال ناشىء عن استحقاق شرعي فطري

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet declared people's blood and property inviolable; Ibn Ashur likens unlawful seizure of property to bloodshed because both provoke internecine violence and loss.
rows.anchor: ومن أجل ذلك قرن الأموال بالدماء في خطبة حجة الوداع إذ قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking property without right invites attacks and plunder; obtaining it without God's approval is ingratitude that exposes it to divine punishment and loss.
rows.anchor: انتزاع الأموال بدون وجهها يفضي إلى التواثب والتثاور فتكون معرضة للابتزاز والزوال

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء الله
rows.claim: Ibn Ata Allah says the ungrateful expose blessings to loss, while gratitude binds them securely.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء الله : ( من لم يشكر النعم فقد تعرض لزوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enduring reward is everlasting bliss, as in 19:76, where lasting good deeds bring a better reward and return with the Lord.
rows.anchor: وأما كونه أخرويا فلأن نهي الله عنها مقارن للوعد بالجزاء على تركها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqiyya may also mean virtue, good, or blessing: what is preserved is precious, as in 2:248 and in this verse's people who forbid corruption.
rows.anchor: على أن لفظ ( البقية ) يحتمل معنى آخر من الفضل في كلام العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mashhud can describe something widely witnessed because it is famous; Umm Qays al-Dabiyya's poem illustrates that sense, linked to 4:41–42.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المشهود بمعنى كثير الشاهدين إياه لشهرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The postponement clause interrupts the account of the gathered Day to answer deniers who imagine their disbelief should anger God into hastening resurrection; God set its due date when creating the world, as He sets lifespans, parallel to 34:29–30.
rows.anchor: والمقصود الرد على المنكرين للبعث مستدلين بتأخير وقوعه في حين تكذيبهم به يحسبون أن تكذيبهم به يغيظ الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajal can mean either the period allowed for a matter or its endpoint; the preposition here indicates the endpoint, as in 7:34.
rows.anchor: والأجل : أصله المدة المنظر إليها في أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma'dud literally means counted and implies a precise fixed term that cannot shift, or serves as a euphemism for its nearness.
rows.anchor: والمعدود : أصله المحسوب ، وأطلق هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence elaborates on the Day when people are gathered in 11:103: its central point is that people divide into the wretched and fortunate, while the opening prepares by evoking the Day's gravity.
rows.anchor: جملة { يوم يأتي لا تكلم نفس } تفصيل لمدلول جملة { ذلك يوم مجموع له الناس }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm can mean a moment or time rather than an entire day; the Nabigha uses “day” with “daylight hours,” and Tawba ibn al-Humayyir uses “night” for the hour of departure or return.
rows.anchor: وهو استعمال شائع في الكلام العربي في لفظ ( يوم ) و ( ليلة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It comes” refers to the witnessed Day of 11:103—Resurrection—and means that it occurs and arrives, as in 43:66.
rows.anchor: وضمير ( يأتي ) عائد إلى { يوم مشهود } ( هود : 103 ) وهو يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm is an adverb attached to “no soul speaks”; the sentence begins anew with the time expression fronted, meaning no one speaks when the witnessed Day arrives.
rows.anchor: ظرف متعلق بقوله : { لا تكلم نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to God, who alone permits speech, as in 78:38; this refutes pagan belief that idols have a right to intercede.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنه لا يتكلم أحد إلا بإذن من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under negation, nafs includes every soul, righteous and sinful, and all speech, including an intercessor's words and a person's argument for themself.
rows.anchor: و { نفس } يعم جميع النفوس لوقوعه في سياق النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The division into wretched and fortunate details the assembled people of 11:103, with its placement after the parenthetical postponement preserving a carefully arranged discourse.
rows.anchor: وهذا التفصيل مفيد تفصيل الناس في قوله : { مجموع له الناس }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaqi is an adjective describing someone immersed in wretchedness: a bad, harsh condition that conflicts with the person's nature.
rows.anchor: والشقي : فعيل صفة مشبهة من شقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sa'id is the opposite: a person immersed in felicity, enjoying good and pleasant conditions; here one faces punishment and hardship, another bliss and ease.
rows.anchor: والسعيد : ضد الشقي ، وهو المتلبس بالسعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wretchedness and felicity have many gradations; this verse summarizes the distinction developed in the following descriptions of the two groups.
rows.anchor: والشقاوة والسعادة من المواهي المقولة بالتشكيك فكلتاهما مراتب كثيرة متفاوتة في قوة الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zafir is forceful exhalation under respiratory pressure; shahiq is its opposite, a strained drawing of air into the chest from urgent need to breathe.
rows.anchor: والزفير : إخراج الأنفاس بدفع وشدة بسبب ضغط التنفس . والشهيق : عكسه وهو اجتلاب الهواء إلى الصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse singles out these disfiguring breaths to deter people from the causes of damnation; their ugliness frightens more than a bare mention of pain.
rows.anchor: وخص بالذكر من أحوالهم في جهنم الزفير والشهيق تنفيرا من أسباب المصير إلى النار
